modes: SP2V_LOGIC_HIGH (per-bit compile-time, selects p or n variant)

guarantees.claim: For each i in 0..Sp2VWidth-1, if SP2V_LOGIC_HIGH[i]==1, an aes_control_fsm_p instance is connected to all listed ports; otherwise an aes_control_fsm_n instance is connected.
All listed output signals (e.g., mr_alert[i]) are directly driven by the corresponding instance output port (alert_o, etc.) with per-bit indexing; no logic is inserted in this chunk.
The start_i port of the FSM instance is connected to the internal signal start_trigger, not the top-level start_i.
The key_init_qe_i port is connected to the internal signal int_key_init_qe, not a direct top-level input.

assumptions.claim: The signal start_trigger is correctly generated by surrounding logic to pulse when start_i is asserted and all gating conditions are met, effectively starting the FSM.
assumptions.cond: when the FSM is expected to start
assumptions.risk: If start_trigger is stuck low or not pulsed correctly, all FSM instances never activate, causing the AES engine to hang and output data never be produced.

assumptions.claim: The sparsified input signals (e.g., sp_cipher_in_ready[i], sp_cipher_out_valid[i], sp_in_cipher_crypt[i], int_ctr_we[i], etc.) are driven by logic that maintains the sparse encoding (likely one-hot or dual-rail) expected by the FSM.
assumptions.risk: Corruption of the sparse encoding (e.g., illegal multi-bit pattern) may cause the FSM to enter an undefined state, bypassing fault detection and potentially leading to key exposure or incorrect encryption.

uncertain_points.claim: The AND/OR/AND-combine and OR-combine annotations indicate that the final control signals (like ctrl_we, alert, start_we, etc.) are derived by combining all per-instance bits outside this chunk. The combining logic is not shown; if it uses a wrong operation (e.g., AND instead of OR) or omits bits, a single faulty instance may not be detected, defeating the sparse FSM fault tolerance.
uncertain_points.cond: where annotation is OR-combine or AND-combine
uncertain_points.risk: A fault in one FSM instance may be masked (if wrongly ANDed) or erroneously trigger an alert (if wrongly ORed). In the worst case, an attacker-induced fault could go undetected, compromising the security of the AES operation.

uncertain_points.claim: The sparse FSM selection vector SP2V_LOGIC_HIGH is presumably a compile-time constant that spreads high bits across the Sp2VWidth to create a unique encoding. The origin and correctness of this vector are not visible; if it is malformed (e.g., too few high bits or uneven distribution), the fault coverage of the sparse FSM may be reduced, potentially allowing biased faults to go undetected.
uncertain_points.risk: Reduced fault detection capability, making the AES engine susceptible to fault attacks that could leak key material or produce incorrect ciphertext without raising an alert.

uncertain_points.claim: The internal signal int_key_init_qe (connected to key_init_qe_i) is generated elsewhere; its timing and behavior relative to key loading and the FSM state are unknown. If int_key_init_qe is asserted at an unsafe time (e.g., while a key clear operation is in progress), it could cause a key exposure or corrupt the key state.
uncertain_points.risk: Improper sequencing of key_init_qe could lead to key material being read while partially cleared or written in an uncontrolled manner, compromising key confidentiality.
